decisions.question: LKG update mechanism: when a full test run passes, how should `.egg/last-known-good` be updated on the working branch?

options.label: Ride-along on the next commit the agent/developer makes (no dedicated commit; .egg/last-known-good is staged by `make test-all` and gets swept up naturally) — recommended
Auto-commit immediately on every green `make test-all` (one dedicated commit per full-run pass; clean signal but history noise and gateway-policy friction)
Amend onto the HEAD commit that triggered the run (no extra commit but rewrites history — dangerous default)
Manual-only: `make test-record-good` is the ONLY way the file advances (zero automation; agents / devs must remember to run it)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Other: Automatic write to the sidecar file (.egg-state/last-known-good/<branch>.sha) after every green `make test-all` pass — no commit involved since decision-10 = sidecar. `make test-record-good` is the manual override. Commit-based options don't apply under sidecar storage."}

decisions.question: CI integration: how should CI `.github/workflows/test.yml` interact with the new changeset-aware behavior, given CI already enforces `--cov-fail-under=80` via `PYTEST_ARGS`?

options.label: Switch CI to `make test-all` — preserves the 80% coverage gate as-is; `make test` stays the agent/dev fast path. (Recommended)
Keep CI on `make test`, and have `make test` auto-degrade to a full run whenever `--cov` appears in `PYTEST_ARGS` (coverage-aware fallback)
Keep CI on `make test` with narrowed selection; drop `--cov-fail-under=80` on PR runs and enforce it only on `main` nightly / merge-queue
Keep CI on `make test` with narrowed selection; keep coverage gate but scope it to changed files only (`--cov` on selected dirs)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Switch CI to `make test-all` — preserves the 80% coverage gate as-is; `make test` stays the agent/dev fast path. (Recommended)"}

decisions.question: Test-selection tooling: which approach should the plan phase design around?

options.label: Static reverse import-graph via `grimp` (maintained, Rust-backed, has `find_downstream_modules`; adds one dev dep) — recommended
Coverage-based selection via `pytest-testmon` (finer granularity, catches dynamic imports on executed paths; requires prior full run; fragile with `pytest-cov`)
Hybrid: `grimp` for file-level selection + `pytest-testmon` for intra-file narrowing (two dependencies, more moving parts)
Path-mapping (Airflow-style hand-curated dir→dir map in YAML; zero graph dependency; coarser; doesn't meet leaf-module acceptance criterion)
Hand-rolled static graph using Python stdlib `ast` (no new dependency; reinvents grimp; more code to maintain)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Static reverse import-graph via `grimp` (maintained, Rust-backed, has `find_downstream_modules`; adds one dev dep) — recommended"}

decisions.question: `.egg/last-known-good` file format

options.label: Bare 40-char sha (one-line file; simplest; no parsing cost) — recommended
Structured JSON with {sha, env_digest, updated_at} (richer invalidation; slightly larger surface)
Bare sha + a separate `.egg/last-known-good.invalidated` marker file when fallback triggers fire (two files; explicit)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Bare 40-char sha (one-line file; simplest; no parsing cost) — recommended"}

decisions.question: Non-Python resource fallback trigger policy (v1): when a non-`.py` file changes in the diff, how should test selection behave?

options.label: Any non-`.py` change → full suite (simple, conservative, no allowlist maintenance) — recommended for v1

Explicit allowlist of test-relevant non-`.py` paths (shared/prompts/, shared/egg_anchor/schemas/, tests/action/, tests/workflows/, tests/config/) → full suite; all other non-`.py` changes skip the trigger
Map each non-`.py` resource directory to the tests that exercise it, and include those tests without triggering a full suite (fine-grained; requires hand-maintained map)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Any non-`.py` change → full suite (simple, conservative, no allowlist maintenance) — recommended for v1"}

decisions.question: Merge behavior implementation: how should `.egg/last-known-good` be rewritten to `main`'s pre-merge HEAD on merge?

options.label: Merge-queue step / GitHub Action that rewrites the file as part of the merge commit (requires merge-queue infra) — recommended if available
Gateway-enforced server-side pre-push hook on pushes to `main` that rewrites the file
Squash-merge only for the egg repo — rely on squash to drop branch LKG history and have a post-merge workflow reset the file on `main`
Don't rewrite; leave LKG as-is and accept that branches cut from main may inherit stale-but-valid values
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Don't rewrite; leave LKG as-is and accept that branches cut from main may inherit stale-but-valid values"}

decisions.question: Naming: what should the full-suite escape-hatch target be called?

options.label: `make test-all` (matches the issue's proposal; the default `make test` becomes changeset-aware) — recommended
Rename current target: `make test` = changeset-aware (new), `make test-full` = full suite
Keep `make test` = full suite (status quo) and add `make test-fast` as the new changeset-aware target (less risky; no behavior change on default target)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "`make test-all` (matches the issue's proposal; the default `make test` becomes changeset-aware) — recommended"}

decisions.question: Gateway / role policy for `.egg/last-known-good` pushes

options.label: Add `.egg/last-known-good` to the push allowlist for every role that runs `make test` (refiner, planner, coder, tester, reviewers, …) — broad but simple. Recommended.

Route LKG updates through a gateway-side observer: the sandbox never writes the file directly; the gateway observes a passing full-run signal (e.g. via a structured pytest report) and commits LKG itself on the agent's branch.
Restrict LKG writes to a dedicated 'test-runner' role only — means other roles can't update LKG, so the file only advances when that role runs tests.
Make the file untracked (.gitignore) and accept the loss of cross-sandbox continuity — sidesteps gateway policy entirely.
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Make the file untracked (.gitignore) and accept the loss of cross-sandbox continuity — sidesteps gateway policy entirely."}

decisions.question: LKG storage medium: where should the last-known-good sha live?

options.label: Non-tracked sidecar in `.egg-state/last-known-good/<branch>.sha` (gitignored; per-branch; no merge/history noise; analysis-recommended) — flips the issue's default
Tracked file `.egg/last-known-good` (the issue's proposal; cross-sandbox portable; auto-commits interact with gateway role-boundary rules)
Git notes on `refs/notes/egg-lkg` (invisible to diff/history; requires fetch/push of notes; gateway has no existing policy for notes)
Abandon LKG entirely — always baseline on `$(BASE_BRANCH)` (simplest; loses the narrow-diff-after-many-local-commits benefit)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Non-tracked sidecar in `.egg-state/last-known-good/<branch>.sha` (gitignored; per-branch; no merge/history noise; analysis-recommended) — flips the issue's default"}

decisions.question: Dynamic-import handling: how should the selector widen for `importlib` / `__import__` / `SourceFileLoader` / entry-point plugins?

options.label: Grep-and-widen: if any changed file contains a dynamic-import pattern, fall back to full suite (blunt but simple) — recommended for v1
Scan during graph construction: record which modules contain dynamic-import patterns; widen only if a changed module is in (or reachable from) that set — more targeted
Runtime import-hook on a seed full-run: instrument the initial `make test-all` to record runtime import edges and persist them alongside the graph
Shadow-imports file (Qik `qikimports.py` style): hand-maintained list of known dynamic edges, consulted at graph-build time
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Scan during graph construction: record which modules contain dynamic-import patterns; widen only if a changed module is in (or reachable from) that set — more targeted"}

decisions.question: CI checkout depth: `actions/checkout@v4` uses `fetch-depth: 1` today, so `origin/main` isn't locally available for `git diff`. How should the implementation handle this?

options.label: Deepen checkout to `fetch-depth: 0` in `.github/workflows/test.yml` (always have full history; simplest) — recommended
Fetch the baseline ref on demand inside `make test` (wrap in a helper; keeps CI checkout shallow)
Require callers to have the baseline already fetched; fall back to full suite when absent (no CI change; no extra git ops)
Not an issue if CI uses `make test-all` (decision-2) — only `make test` needs the baseline
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Not an issue if CI uses `make test-all` (decision-2) — only `make test` needs the baseline"}

decisions.question: Graph granularity: at what level should the reverse-closure be computed?

options.label: Module-level (grimp default; one node per import-resolvable module; sufficient for file-level test selection) — recommended
File-level (one node per `.py` file; redundant when modules and files are 1:1, potentially useful for `__init__.py` changes)
Function-level (requires `pyan` or `pytest-testmon`; enables intra-file narrowing at the cost of adding a dynamic tool)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Module-level (grimp default; one node per import-resolvable module; sufficient for file-level test selection) — recommended"}

Simpler.", "Q14": "Absent sidecar = 'no LKG, use base branch.' No bootstrap ceremony. Every branch starts without an LKG and advances its own as `make test-all` passes.", "Q15": "Both: human-readable log line to stderr on every `make test` invocation, plus a JSON record at `.egg-state/selection/<sha>.json` for post-hoc analysis. Plan phase should refine this by inspecting which `shared/tests/` files are actually consumed as cross-package fixtures vs. being self-contained tests.

questions.question: Fallback-trigger list completeness: review the recommended set (any `conftest.py` change; `Makefile`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`; `.github/workflows/test.yml`; dynamic-import-touched files; unresolvable baseline; non-`.py` changes per decision-5). Anything missing or overreaching?
questions.answer: Accept the listed set (any conftest.py change, Makefile, pyproject.toml, uv.lock, .github/workflows/test.yml, dynamic-import-touched files, unresolvable baseline, non-.py changes per decision-6). Add: `.python-version` (interpreter pin). Nothing listed looks like overreach.

questions.question: Canary mode: every Nth `make test` run on a branch (or once per day) forces a full suite to catch cases where static selection silently misses a test. Do we want this, and at what cadence?
questions.answer: Yes, canary mode. Every 10th invocation on a branch forces a full suite (cheap silent-miss insurance). Cadence and keying (per-branch counter) settle in plan phase.

questions.question: Explicit pytest args: how should `make test` behave when invoked with explicit paths/args (e.g., `make test PYTEST_ARGS='gateway/tests/test_specific.py'`) — bypass narrowing (dev override), intersect, or union?
questions.answer: Intersect by default: narrow to the selected set, then apply user's `-k`/path args within that set. Bypass narrowing only when the user passes explicit test file paths (e.g. `make test PYTEST_ARGS='gateway/tests/test_specific.py'`) — that's an unambiguous dev override.

questions.question: Introspection `--why`: should the implementation surface why a test was selected (print import chain from changed module → test)? Useful for agents diagnosing 'I expected this test to run and it didn't.'
questions.answer: Yes, `--why <test>` that prints the import chain from changed module → test. Debuggability beats terseness; agents will need this.

questions.question: Fallback-cause printing: when `make test` falls back to full suite due to a trigger file change, should it print which trigger caused it, or is a generic message sufficient?
questions.answer: Explicit trigger identification. 'Falling back: Makefile changed' is far more useful than 'Falling back' when an agent wonders why its narrow change pulled in the full suite.

questions.question: Testmon follow-up appetite: appetite for adding `pytest-testmon` in a follow-up issue (intra-file narrowing), or close the door on dynamic selection entirely?
questions.answer: Yes, leave a follow-up issue open for pytest-testmon experimentation once we have real static-selection miss-rate data. Do not close the door on dynamic selection.

questions.question: Parallel agents: two sandboxes running `make test-all` on the same branch race on LKG updates. Last-writer-wins is safe (both shas represent green states) but can churn the file. Acceptable, or need explicit coordination (per-agent sidecar, lock, merge logic)?
questions.answer: Last-writer-wins is acceptable. Sidecar is per-branch; parallel sandboxes on the same branch are rare; both shas represent green states so neither is incorrect. No coordination needed.

questions.question: Integration / e2e / security test targets are out of scope per the issue. Confirm they stay full-suite-only for this PR, or should they be considered for a follow-up issue?
questions.answer: Stay full-suite-only for integration/e2e/security in this PR. Those targets are explicitly out of scope per the issue. If narrowing them is valuable, it's a follow-up issue.

questions.question: Documentation placement: the repo has no `docs/guides/testing.md` today. Preferred location — update `CONTRIBUTING.md`, create new `docs/guides/testing.md`, update `make help`, or some combination?
questions.answer: Create `docs/guides/testing.md` as the canonical doc. Add a one-line summary to `make help` output. Add a pointer from `CONTRIBUTING.md` (one line + link to the guide). Matches the existing docs/guides/ convention.

questions.question: Partial-pass LKG behavior: issue says 'never updated on a partial pass.' Confirm that's still the intent (no, even cheap no-op-style writes) under the chosen LKG storage/update mechanism.
questions.answer: Confirmed: never update LKG on a partial (changeset-aware) pass. With sidecar + auto-update gated on `make test-all`, this invariant holds naturally.

questions.question: Read-only agent phases: some agent roles have `.egg-readonly` markers. Should those roles READ LKG (to compute the baseline) but never WRITE it, or accept that they always fall back to base-branch baseline?
questions.answer: Read-only agent phases (refiner, reviewer_*) always fall back to the base-branch baseline. They don't run `make test-all`, so they have no LKG to update, and reading a stale cross-sandbox sidecar would be more confusing than useful. Simpler.

questions.question: Bootstrap / first-use: how do we initialize LKG on branches that predate this change (including main's first commit under the new scheme)? Checked-in default, empty, or absent treated as 'no LKG, use base branch'?
questions.answer: Absent sidecar = 'no LKG, use base branch.' No bootstrap ceremony. Every branch starts without an LKG and advances its own as `make test-all` passes.

questions.question: Selection-decision logging: stderr always, JSON file at `.egg-state/selection/<sha>.json`, or both?
questions.answer: Both: human-readable log line to stderr on every `make test` invocation, plus a JSON record at `.egg-state/selection/<sha>.json` for post-hoc analysis. Structured log is cheap and pays off whenever something looks wrong.

questions.question: Worktree keying: in worktree scenarios (agents on multiple branches in parallel), is a sidecar file keyed by `<branch>` sufficient, or do we need keying by worktree path too?
questions.answer: `<branch>` key is sufficient for v1. Parallel worktrees on the same branch are rare enough that last-writer-wins (Q9) handles it. If we see pathological churn later, revisit with worktree-path keying.
